## TL;DR

Checks tab navigation completed successfully in a component interaction pass. The view switched through Now, Runs, Test suite and Check plan, and each click updated both the selected tab and the `?tab=` route value. No application stall reproduced, so there was no product defect to fix. I added a regression test for the click-through path. A live visual pass at desktop and phone widths could not be completed because the computer-use browser host was unavailable in this session; consequently, the original slowdown cannot be conclusively attributed to the browser capture harness. The required scoped RepoOS check passed, including its remote build, changed tests, browser smoke gate and local guards.

## Work and rationale

I first inspected the task specification and the Checks view’s tab wiring. Tabs are buttons rendered in a tablist; each invokes `setTab`, which replaces the route query. The view also performs asynchronous data refreshes on mount and on route query changes. This made direct tab interaction, with no repeated screenshot calls, the useful reproduction for distinguishing a navigation stall from a capture-loop slowdown.

I attempted to use the available computer-use browser integration to inspect the live app. The browser access host returned “unavailable” before any tab could be opened. I did not treat that infrastructure failure as evidence of a Checks page failure, and I did not claim responsive viewport behavior from it.

To exercise navigation without screenshots, I extended the existing Checks view test. The test starts at Now, clicks each of the four visible tab controls in sequence, waits for Vue/router updates, then confirms the route query and `aria-selected` control match the requested tab. That sequence passed. Existing tests in the same suite also cover direct links, the default route behavior, and the plan tab’s rendering and refresh behavior.

Because the direct click-through did not reproduce a stall, there was no app fix to make. The additional test records the successful interaction behavior so a future change that breaks route-based tab selection is caught. It intentionally does not assert a browser or screenshot-capture performance diagnosis.

I ran `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. The first attempt was interrupted when the session ended before completion, and the automatic handoff reported the missing engineering report draft. On retry, remote validation passed after waiting for an available runner slot. It built the branch, ran the changed and always-run tests, and passed the headless browser gate. Local formatting, lint, build, CSS safeguards, rendered contrast, branch-artifact checks and UI smoke all passed as well.

## Approaches tried

- Inspected the task and Checks view implementation to identify what navigation state should change on each tab click.
- Attempted live browser access through the computer-use host. The host was unavailable, so no live page interaction or viewport resize could be performed.
- Ran the existing focused Checks test file, including its new sequential click-through coverage. All cases passed.
- Ran the required changed-path RepoOS check. The incremental remote bundle initially had no usable base, so RepoOS retried with a full bundle. On the subsequent check attempt, a runner slot was busy; RepoOS waited, then completed validation successfully.

## Challenges and blockers

The material limitation is the unavailable browser access host. The user’s acceptance criteria ask for live verification at representative desktop and narrow widths. This session verified the tab state and route interaction in the Vue test environment, and the required headless smoke gate passed, but neither result proves the visual layout at 1440px or phone widths. I cannot conclude from this evidence alone that the original slowness was definitely in repeated screenshot capture. The narrower conclusion is that direct component-level tab navigation did not stall and there is no reproduced app fault.

## Key learnings

For reports of a browser pass slowing during repeated capture, direct interactions without capture are a distinct diagnostic step. Here, sequential tab clicks and route updates completed normally, which weakens the case for an app navigation regression. The live capture-harness comparison remains unobserved because the browser host itself was unavailable. The passing remote browser smoke gate gives useful general coverage, but it is not a substitute for the requested multi-width, multi-theme visual pass.
